answer: Each identity must hold a licensed perfusionist registration, earned with supervised clinical perfusion hours and a board exam costing about $250 per candidate. A farm needs a distinct licensed perfusionist per fake, so 1,000 fakes cost $250,000 plus years of clinical hours each. The dune of cheap aliases shifts: every fake adds another exam, the marble of the board register exposes shared credentials, and the willow of scale bends under training time.
